rules.basis: National Dietary Guidelines for Bangladesh 2025, Guideline 2 (diabetes mellitus), p.69: "Sodium restriction varies with individual health status, usually in a range of <2000 mg/day is recommended" (verified verbatim against the downloaded PDF on 2026-11-14; printed p.69 = PDF p.91). Caution/avoid fractions (0.3/0.6) are SafePlate heuristics, not from the guideline.

National Dietary Guidelines for Bangladesh 2025, Guideline 7 (hypertension), p.81: "sodium <1.5 g" (with fibre 30 g, cholesterol 150 mg) and "Reduce salt intake to less than 1tsp/day, preferably three-quarters of a teaspoon/day" (verified verbatim against the downloaded PDF on 2026-11-14; printed p.81 = PDF p.103). The source itself states both sodium <1.5 g and salt under 1 tsp (about 2000 mg sodium) - the inconsistency is in the source; the quote is faithful. Caution/avoid fractions (0.3/0.6) are SafePlate heuristics, not from the guideline.

National Dietary Guidelines for Bangladesh 2025, Guideline 2 (diabetes mellitus), p.68: "Use low fat and fat free cooking methods such as boiling, steaming, broiling, baking, roasting and grilling" (verified verbatim against the downloaded PDF on 2026-11-14; printed p.68 = PDF p.90). Restricting fat and oil and the higher coronary risk of people with diabetes are stated in the same chapter.

National Dietary Guidelines for Bangladesh 2025, Guideline 2 (fats and oils), p.19: "Limit the intake of deep-fried foods and oily snacks" (verified verbatim against the downloaded PDF on 2026-11-14; printed p.19 = PDF p.41). The same page limits trans-fat foods including fried and processed items. The document has two different chapters both numbered Guideline 2 (fats/oils and diabetes); the page numbers disambiguate them.
